what: WHAT SKETCH-LIKE OR CONCEPT-LIKE MATERIAL THIS ARCHIVE HOLDS, and which of it may honestly be shown as one. Written 19 August 2026 for the owner's direction of the same day: place sketches and unfinished pieces 'strictly where it fits only'. This register answers the question that direction raises and no existing register answers -- is a holding sketch-grade, and may it be published as a sketch -- and it answers it for every holding the archive has, including the ones the answer is NO for.
reading: THIS IS AN INDEX OF HOLDINGS, NOT A SECOND PROVENANCE RECORD. Hand, licence and subject are owned by site/arda_assets.json for published files and by site/arda_heraldry_assets.json for devices; where a holding has an owning register this file NAMES it in `register` and repeats only enough to be read alone. arda_plates.json's own note states the trap this avoids in its own words: a second place for a fact to go stale. Nothing here binds a picture to a route -- that is arda_plates.json's job and this file must never grow one.
shape: One row per HOLDING -- a directory or a class of material -- not per file, because 754 ornament fragments already have a register of their own and copying them here would be the duplication above. Fields are the union of the two existing asset registers and nothing new: `file`, `what`, `hand`, `licence`, `source` from arda_assets.json; `publishable`, `why_not` from arda_heraldry_assets.json. `n`, `sketchlike`, `why_sketchlike` and `register` are this file's own and carry its whole reason for existing.
the_licence_position: STATED PLAINLY BECAUSE IT DECIDES EVERY ROW, AND IN TWO PARTS THAT MUST NOT BE CONFLATED. (A) THE LAW, WHICH NOBODY HERE CAN CHANGE. No meaningful corpus of openly-licensed Tolkien-world art exists. Nothing of Tolkien's own enters the public domain before 1 January 2044 in any jurisdiction this archive is likely to be read in. The Tolkien Estate's own FAQ extends its refusal to charitable and not-for-profit use in terms, so the archive's non-commercial character buys it nothing. Tolkien Gateway relicensed its TEXT to CC BY-SA 4.0 on 1 January 2025; its IMAGES are individually copyright-reserved and the fair-use claim under which it hosts them is tied to that site and does not travel. John Howe's and Alan Lee's work is comprehensively in copyright and both are living. (B) THE ARCHIVE'S RECORDED BASIS, WHICH IS THE OWNER'S WORD AND IS RECORDED AS HIS RULING RATHER THAN AS A LICENCE ANY FILE STATES. His standing authorization of 16 August 2026: 'we have the right and authorization to use and publish everything and anything we have or find'. CLAUDE.md records exactly what that does and does not do: it answers MAY WE PUBLISH IT and it does not answer WHOSE IS IT; the tiers are untouched; and refusal by name survives intact. (C) WHAT STILL REFUSES, UNDER THE OWNER'S OWN EARLIER AND UNREPEALED RULINGS. The artwork ruling of 29 July 2026 stands for Tolkien's and Christopher Tolkien's ARTWORK: it is not republished, and the heraldry hall's the-device-Tolkien-himself-drew mark is named in that ruling as the case it was made to agree with. THEREFORE, on the owner's direction of 19 August to work in Howe's and Lee's style: that can only mean ORIGINAL WORK BY THIS ARCHIVE IN A COMPATIBLE IDIOM, LABELLED AS THE ARCHIVE'S OWN. It may never mean reproducing, tracing, recreating or generating-from their images. The archive may publish its own MEASUREMENTS of their published linework -- density, stroke weight, tonal range, palette -- as DATA with attribution, because a measurement is not a reproduction; that is the boundary the owner set on 1 August 2026 for Christopher Tolkien's hand and it holds here for the same reason. It may cite their COMMENTARY, which site/arda_sources.json already rules for the Alan Lee sketchbook in its own words: what the archive may use is his commentary, with the picture named and not shown.
the_tool_notice: Every generated plate this archive publishes carries the owner's mandatory notice of 13 August 2026 naming the tool that made it. `hand` on such a row reads GENERATED and names the model; 'unknown' is not an answer ruling 3 accepts and 'generated' is.
the_verdict_on_sketch_as_a_tier_MARKER: The proposal tested on 19 August was that a finished plate stands where the corpus is firm and a SKETCH stands where the archive is inferring or the texts disagree. Measured over all 582 entity routes: 43 (7.4%) print an [I-*] marker, 25 (4.3%) rest on no tier-1 attestation at all, and the union is 68 (11.7%) with ZERO overlap between the two. The disagreement half cannot be built: the archive records 17 contradictions in total, in arda_contradictions.json, and not one of them is bound to any route -- there is no per-entity disagreement field, and asserting one would be a silence nothing searched for. What IS well populated is the WEIGHT of attestation: 79 routes rest on two or fewer tier-1 lines, 340 on three to five, 163 on six or more. So finish grades attestation weight, which is printed on the same leaf and can be checked; and a genuinely open, unfinished drawing is reserved for the 82 routes (14.1%) for which the archive holds no plate at all, where 'unfinished' is a true statement about the archive rather than a symbolic one about the corpus. The full argument is in the heraldry chain's report.

refuses.a picture of Tolkien's or Christopher To: the owner's ruling of 29 July 2026. Reference copies are held, gitignored, and never enter site/.
refuses.a picture of Howe's or Lee's hand: their copyright is live and a living illustrator's is a stronger reason than the 29 July ruling, not a weaker one -- site/arda_sources.json says so on the Alan Lee row.
refuses.a sketch generated FROM a named artist's: a derivative is not an original, whatever made it; the compatible-idiom permission above is a permission to draw, not to imitate a specific hand.
refuses.binding any holding here to a route: arda_plates.json owns bindings; a second binder is a second place for a fact to go stale.
refuses.an ornament captioned as an illustration: uploads/ornament/MANIFEST.json rules this in its own words -- binding an acanthus spray to Weathertop would be a claim about what Weathertop looked like.

holdings.what: centreline traces of Christopher Tolkien's map plates -- one open path per pen stroke, 4,974 to 62,646 paths each
holdings.hand: Christopher Tolkien drew the linework; the tracing is the archive's own, by map/gen_centerline.py
holdings.licence: published at the owner's explicit direction, 1 August 2026. NOT a grant from the rightsholder and not recorded as one.
holdings.why_sketchlike: THIS IS THE ARCHIVE'S ONE EXISTING PUBLISHED ARTEFACT THAT IS ALREADY A SKETCH, and it did not set out to be. A centreline extraction is line without fill, weight or wash -- which is exactly what a drawn sketch is. It is also the archive's own measurement rather than his image, which is why it may be shown at all. Anything the archive publishes as a sketch should look like this and be defensible on the same ground.

holdings.file: (no file -- drawn live by the forge from a spec in heraldry.js)
holdings.what: the archive's own computed heraldic devices, arrangement and tinctures measured off the plates
holdings.hand: this archive's forge, map/forge_*.py and the renderer in site/heraldry.js
holdings.why_sketchlike: THE FORGE ALREADY HAS A SKETCH DIAL AND NOBODY CALLED IT ONE. `hand` (0..1) wobbles every radius, width and bearing a course repeats; `tone` and `grain` shade a fill within one shape and vary each repeat, as a hand-coloured row of petals varies. All three are seeded from the course and item index and from nothing else -- no clock, no random number -- so a device draws identically every time. 18 of the 50 already carry hand>=0.5 and 10 carry tone. This is the archive's cleanest route to sketch-grade art of ANY device: it is parametric, deterministic, entirely the archive's own code, and it needs no new licence because it needs no new picture.

holdings.hand: this archive's own; drawn as geometry, not traced

It COULD be rendered sketch-grade by stripping fills to strokes, and that would be the archive's own choice about its own art with no licence question at all -- but as it stands it is a finished plate and must not be captioned as a sketch.

holdings.what: illustrated reconstructions of devices, cropped to the device by map/gen_illustrated_devices.py and shown in the hall
holdings.hand: unattributed (20); Rondador Nocturno, identified by the monogram on his plate (1)
holdings.licence: the owner's standing authorization of 16 August 2026 -- the same basis the archive records for everything it publishes without a stated third-party licence. 20 rows read: unattributed; rights confirmed by the site's owner; 1 reads: NOT ESTABLISHED -- the plate carries the monogram of Rondador Nocturno, so it is not unattributed and no licence is on record".
holdings.why_not: PUBLISHED, AND THE FINDING IS NOT THAT THEY LACK A BASIS. The owner's 16 August authorization is the basis, and it is his to give. TWO THINGS ARE NEVERTHELESS WRONG AND BOTH ARE CHECKABLE. FIRST, THE HALL'S OWN LEGEND OVERSTATES THEM TO A READER. heraldry.html describes every mark-artwork device as: a device Tolkien designed, shown as a freely-licensed recreation (Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA / Public Domain, attributed below). Measured 19 August: 17 devices are shown from an SVG and those 17 do carry a free licence -- CC BY-SA 3.0 x9, Public domain x5, CC BY-SA 4.0 x3. The 21 shown from heraldry/illustrated/*.png carry none, and 20 of them are not from Commons at all but 'supplied to the workshop, 2026-07-25/26'. The legend is a claim about provenance made to a reader, and for 21 of 38 displayed files it is not what the register says. SECOND, THE HAND IS UNKNOWN FOR 20 OF THE 21. CLAUDE.md is explicit that the authorization settles publication and never authorship, and ruling 3 requires the hand and refuses a guess in it. 'unattributed' is an honest record of an absence and it is not an answer to 'whose is it'. NOTHING IS WITHDRAWN BY THIS FILE and nothing should be withdrawn on inference -- that register is not this chain's to edit, and the owner has ruled twice that un-withdrawing and withdrawing published artwork are both his calls. The repair that needs no ruling is the legend.
holdings.why_sketchlike: finished painted illustration, and the last material in the archive that should be roughened -- altering it would make a derivative of a work whose rights are already unestablished.

holdings.what: harvested ornament fragments -- 51 initials, 45 line-fillers, 32 decorated initials, 19 birds, 16 trees, 15 marks and the rest borders, knots, rosettes and grotesques
holdings.hand: The Walters Art Museum (69), The J. Paul Getty Museum (47), Internet Archive Book Images (490 held / 79 cleared), Bibliotheque nationale de France Gallica (148 held / 15 cleared)
holdings.licence: CC0 (116); No known copyright restrictions, published before 1929 (79); Free for NON-COMMERCIAL reuse under Gallica/BnF conditions (15). 94 of the 210 carry a mandatory credit string that must be printed wherever the fragment is.
holdings.source: uploads/ornament/MANIFEST.json, which carries every fragment's institution, shelfmark, licence, credit and source URL
holdings.why_not: NOT PUBLISHED TODAY, and the bar is the archive's own procedure rather than the licence. uploads/ is gitignored as a class, and that manifest rules that a fragment enters site/ only with a row in arda_assets.json carrying its hand and licence, and only after someone has written what it depicts. 116 are CC0 and need nothing further; 79 are pre-1929 public domain; 15 are Gallica/BnF non-commercial and 94 of the 210 carry a mandatory credit string that must be PRINTED wherever the fragment is shown. So the work owed is the description and the asset row, not a permission.
holdings.why_sketchlike: 131 are medieval illumination and 79 are 19th-century ENGRAVING, which must never be captioned as medieval -- the manifest's own era_warning. THE HARD LIMIT, in the manifest's words: this is ORNAMENT and it does NOT illustrate an entity. It may fill a leaf; it may never stand as a picture of a person, a place or a realm, and it may never be bound in arda_plates.json.

holdings.what: plates of Tolkien's own heraldic devices, held so the forge can measure arrangement and tincture off them
holdings.source: supplied to the workshop; sources/** is gitignored
holdings.register: arda_heraldry_assets.json records the measured OUTPUT; these inputs have no row
holdings.why_not: the owner's ruling of 29 July 2026 -- the archive does not republish Tolkien's artwork. Held to MEASURE from, never to reproduce. Verified 19 August: git check-ignore confirms the class ignore, and no copy exists anywhere under site/.
holdings.why_sketchlike: not the archive's to characterise or to show. What the archive may publish from these is the measurement, and map/detail_metric.py already computes six axes off them -- ink share, distinct colours after a web-safe snap, concentric zones, angular frequency of the ring profile, stroke-width spread, and the share of ink in features under a fiftieth of the radius. THAT MEASUREMENT IS COMPUTED AND NOT PUBLISHED. Publishing it as data with the hand named would be the exact thing the 1 August amendment permits, and no register carries it yet.
